questionText:
Consider the two lists List I and List II given below:

List I List II
(i)    Context free languages (a)    Closed under union
(ii)   Recursive languages (b)    Not closed under complementation
(iii)  Regular languages (c)    Closed under intersection

For matching of items in List I with those in List II, which of the following option(s) is/are CORRECT?
explanation:
Step-by-step Explanation:

1. Analyze Closure Properties:
• (i) Context Free Languages (CFLs):
- CFLs are closed under union.
- CFLs are not closed under complementation.
- CFLs are not closed under intersection.
Therefore, (i) maps uniquely to (b) Not closed under complementation.

• (ii) Recursive Languages:
- Recursive languages are closed under union, complementation, and intersection.
Therefore, (ii) can match with either (a) Closed under union or (c) Closed under intersection.

• (iii) Regular Languages:
- Regular languages are closed under union, complementation, and intersection.
Therefore, (iii) can also match with either (a) Closed under union or (c) Closed under intersection.

2. Evaluate Options:
• Since (i) must map to (b), (ii) and (iii) can share/exchange valid true statements (a) and (c):
- Matching 1: (i) – (b), (ii) – (a), (iii) – (c)  →  Option (B) is valid.
- Matching 2: (i) – (b), (ii) – (c), (iii) – (a)  →  Option (C) is valid.

Hence, Options (B) and (C) are CORRECT.
